headword: {面|つら}の{皮|かわ}が{厚|あつ}い

definitions.explanation: Describes a person who is impervious to embarrassment or criticism, acting without shame even when their behavior is clearly inappropriate. Literally means 'the skin of one's face is thick.'

examples.japanese: あの{人|ひと}は{面|つら}の{皮|かわ}が{厚|あつ}い。
{嘘|うそ}がばれても{平気|へいき}でいられるなんて、{面|つら}の{皮|かわ}が{厚|あつ}い。
examples.english: Being able to stay calm even when caught in a lie — how shameless.

examples.japanese: {自分|じぶん}のミスを{人|ひと}のせいにしておいて、まだ{面|つら}の{皮|かわ}が{厚|あつ}く{居座|いすわ}っている。
examples.english: Even after blaming their own mistakes on others, they're brazenly staying put.

notes:
Literally "the skin of one's face is thick" — a vivid idiom meaning someone is so brazen that criticism bounces right off them. Always used negatively, to criticize someone who acts without shame. The word {面|つら} is a rougher, more colloquial way to say {顔|かお} (face).

USAGE:
Almost always used to criticize or express exasperation at someone's shamelessness. Can be used as a predicate ({面|つら}の{皮|かわ}が{厚|あつ}い) or as a modifier ({面|つら}の{皮|かわ}が{厚|あつ}く...).

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {厚|あつ}かましい: impudent, brazen — a direct adjective meaning shameless; less idiomatic
- {図々|ずうずう}しい: brazen, nervy — similar meaning; slightly more colloquial
- {恥知|はじし}らず: shameless person — a noun directly calling someone shameless
- {鉄面皮|てつめんぴ}: brazen-faced — more literary; literally "iron face skin"
